proposal.thesis: The binding time_box on this Baker Hughes seat has fired. Entry was 2026-07-28 at $58.20 against a plan that required a sustained daily close above $65 within 30 trading days of the 2026-07-27 earnings breakout; the 2026-09-04 weekly review made 2026-09-09 the last extension of that clock. The 2026-09-09 session (prices_meta price_as_of 2026-09-09) printed a high of $66.09 and a close of $63.64 — a tag of $65 that did not hold, on the same day management raised FY2026 sales to $28.5-30.3B and adjusted EBITDA to $4.875-5.475B at the Barclays conference to fold Chart Industries into the model (Reuters / company 8-K 2026-09-09). That raise is real, and 23-analyst mean $72.13 is still 13.3% above $63.70, but the market faded the print (open $63.76, close $63.64, CMF20 -0.105, volume_read neutral) rather than confirming the July breakout the clock was written to catch. Invalidating_print (IET orders / guidance cut) and invalidating_structure (close below $56) did not fire; the chandelier trail at $60.72 is intact with 1.79 ATR of cushion. I am honoring the written clock, not protecting a +9.45% winner. Challenger DELL was considered and is not a swap: 24-analyst mean $564.46 is only +5.4% vs $535.47 and it is the same hyperscaler_server_capex driver as this book's entire realized-loss cluster.
